 Grand Theft Auto 6 begins worldwide release after 13-year wait - and the early reviews are in
 18 November 2026 Summary
 This live page is closed for now - come back later as we cover the UK's midnight release. In the meantime, read more here 
 Grand Theft Auto 6 begins its launch, ending gamers' 13-year wait for a new instalment
 The game is released at midnight around the world, meaning people in New Zealand became the first to play at 11:00 GMT 
 Reviews, so far, give the game a score of 99 , according to Metacritic
 Many critics are praising it as "exquisitely detailed" and "mature" , though some say the game is "inconsistent" and large parts are "boring" 
 The crime game , where players can explore a fictional US state called Leonida, features the series' first playable female protagonist in a 3D setting
 A New Zealand gamer has already finished the introduction - here are his first thoughts (spoiler in post!)
 Warning: some posts on this page contain spoilers - they are labelled at the top 
 Close form Are you playing GTA 6? Share your experiences
 Get in touch Media caption, Watch: Gamers in New Zealand share initial reactions Live Reporting
 Edited by Tinshui Yeung and Joe Coughlan
 New Zealand and Australia gamers praise GTA 6 as UK set for midnight release published at 15:12 GMT 15:12 GMT 
 Joe Coughlan 
Live editor 
 Image source, Reuters Image caption, Australian gamer Asif Mir is among one of the first in the world to be able to play GTA 6
 Grand Theft Auto 6 has begun its phased release to the world, with gamers in New Zealand and Australia praising the software as "amazing" following its local midnight release (11:00 GMT).
 Reviews for the game have been overwhelmingly positive so far, as it maintains an average score of 99 out of 100 on Metacritic .
 Positive write-ups have called the game "a perfect crime", with even the less favourable critics giving the game scores of four out of five and nine out of 10.
 International gamers now continue their 13-year wait for the release - some are even pretending to be hafway across the world to gain access early, our technology reporter Laura Cress reports.
 Later this evening, we will be covering the midnight UK release by speaking to gamers and answering live audience questions with expert journalists and streamers - followed by the first reactions across the country as the nation wakes up to a new era of GTA.
 I will also be bringing you my initial thoughts as I jump into the driver's seat on Thursday morning to try out the game for myself.
 We are pausing our live coverage for now, but you can join us later this evening ahead of the game's UK launch. Read more about initial reactions here.

 GTA 6 is 'the game equivalent of a Christopher Nolan film' published at 14:57 GMT 14:57 GMT 
 Victoriya Holland 
BBC World Service 
 Reece Reilly is a New Zealand-based gamer and podcaster, and interviews game developers and industry figures for his show Kiwi Talkz.
 He’s been playing GTA 6 for over two hours already, and has high praise for the look and feel of the game.
 "The graphics and the art direction, especially are astounding," he tells World Business Express . "I've never seen anything like this in a game. The voice direction is amazing. The music is great. It just feels so good. 
 "I think anybody who liked the previous GTAs will know what they're in for. I think that the thing that's got me the most is just the art and the attention to detail. 
 "You can see where all the investment with the time, the money and the resources. It's like the equivalent of Christopher Nolan, I guess, being able to swing for the fences because he has the resources to do it."

 'That's something I've never really seen before in a video game' - Australian gamer published at 14:41 GMT 14:41 GMT 
 Simon Atkinson 
Reporting from Sydney 
 Spoiler alert: This post contains a few details about the game. 
 It’s 01:00 here in Sydney. Having crashed Andrew Shelley’s apartment for a couple of hours, we’ll leave him to play well into the early hours.
 But what are his first impressions?
 "The thing that's striking me the most is the visuals. It looks stunning and I'm just enjoying kind of how different it feels to previous games, but also with some level of familiarity," he says.
 "I saw a storm for the first time. It looks incredible. The way it kind of envelopes the whole map and feels like a weather system is moving in and it's all localised. That's something I've never really seen before in a video game."
 Andrew says he’s not proud that he’s already pulled the trigger and begun his body count.
 "Maybe I could have been a little more stealthy and survived a little longer without having to shoot. Maybe one day I'll try a pacifist run through the game where I won't have to kill anyone."

 I reviewed GTA 3 25 years ago, when the developers hit a winning formula published at 14:26 GMT 14:26 GMT 
 Daniel Coles 
UK digital editor 
 It was 25 years ago this month that I reviewed GTA 3 for the BBC .
 This was the breakthrough 3D version of the game that propelled its humour, violence and open-world freedom to mainstream attention.
 I called the gameplay a "bloodbath" - it came just weeks after the 9/11 attacks.
 But it was also clear to me and millions of new gamers with their shiny PS2 consoles that the Edinburgh developers had hit a winning formula.
 I thought they might be on GTA 15 by now. But I reckoned without the soaring costs of game development.
 It's remarkable how, like James Bond, it has stayed so beloved by its patient fans - but could it still be around in another 25 years?

 Content creator: GTA 6's female lead shows women 'do belong in the biggest games' published at 14:16 GMT 14:16 GMT 
 Emer Moreau 
 Image source, Paris Karrina It’s no secret that gaming comes with some unflattering stereotypes, including about its treatment of women - both characters in games and female gamers.
 Two women I spoke to, who are eagerly anticipating GTA 6, say they have both been accused of playing video games only to impress others.
 Paris Karrina, a gaming content creator from Newcastle, says she has been accused of being a “pick-me” girl who only posts about gaming “because it’s popular”.
 Karrina says she’s "so happy" that GTA 6 has a female lead because it shows women "do belong in the biggest games, not just on the sidelines".
 Meanwhile, Faith Chika Angel says some people still treat women in gaming as if they “don’t belong”.
 Faith, who makes gaming content under the moniker ChikaCreate, says she understands past criticism of the GTA franchise for its treatment of women.
 “GTA uses a lot of satire and exaggeration, but I don’t think it means its portrayal of women should be beyond criticism.”

 What do other less favourable reviews say? published at 14:01 GMT 14:01 GMT 
 Joe Coughlan 
Live editor 
 Image source, Rockstar Games Reviews have been largely positive for the latest game in the Grand Theft Auto series.
 The lowest-scoring review so far is from ScreenHub .
 The Australia-based publication gave the game four stars out of five, praising it as "lovingly rendered" but saying large sections are "boring and too limited".
 PlayStation LifeStyle gave the game nine out of 10, praising the number of things to do but saying the game's frame rate "frequently" drops and is "inconsistent".
 Gaming news outlet Noisy Pixel also rated the game nine out of 10, calling the protagonists "compelling" but describing the story's pacing as "uneven". It said the system for police responding to criminal actions could feel "unpredictable".

 'A perfect crime' published at 13:31 GMT 13:31 GMT 
 Joe Coughlan 
Live editor 
 Image source, Rockstar Games Reviews are continuing to appear on Metacritic’s list for Grand Theft Auto 6, which is maintaining a score of 99.
 Digital Spy gave the game five stars out of five, saying it surpassed the publication’s “incredibly high expectations” after 200 hours of play.
 US video game magazine Game Informer also gave the game a perfect score of 10 out of 10, saying the relationship between lead characters Lucia and Jason “elevates the game to new heights”.
 Calling the game “a perfect crime”, Paul Tassi of Forbes says in his 10 out of 10 review that the latest instalment is “the most impressive video game world I’ve ever played”.

 GTA 6 holds its 99 score as more reviews come in published at 13:12 GMT 13:12 GMT 
 Tom Gerken 
Technology reporter 
 Earlier this morning, I told you GTA 6 had launched to a near-perfect score from critics.
 According to Metacritic, which aggregates reviews, the game has a 99 out of 100.
 About 50 more reviews have come in since I wrote that, and the score is unchanged. In fact, things might be looking even better.
 Metacritic's overall list , external now puts GTA 6 above Ocarina of Time in its rankings - though it's unclear whether that's because it has a higher average score or if it's simply alphabetical.
 I've asked Metacritic to confirm whether GTA is now officially the best.
 But even if the games are tied at the top, here's something interesting: Zelda got its score back when there weren't many online reviewers. In fact, it scored 99 based on just 22 critic reviews.
 GTA 6 has done it based on 146.

 Gaming the media - how previous GTA releases stirred up fears of violence published at 13:01 GMT 13:01 GMT 
 Imran Rahman-Jones 
Technology reporter 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, GTA 4 - set in New York City - was released in 2008
 Though it’s 18-rated like its predecessors, this may be the first GTA launch where headlines aren’t dominated by concerns about violence.
 Earlier releases were criticised for allegedly glamourising crime, but the controversy was often fuelled by the game’s own creators.
 "The marketing team decided, well you know what, let’s play up this kind of bad boy thing a little bit," the first game’s writer and publicist Brian Baglow told Witness History in 2015.
 The strategy generated huge publicity. Newspapers and even Parliament debated whether it would corrupt the nation’s children.
 "We just did things that we felt were fun," the game’s co-creator Dave Jones told the BBC’s Tech Now programme .
 "We never at any point kind of thought, should we do that? Is it controversial? We never thought that way."

 'I stayed up to play GTA 6 - it did not disappoint' published at 12:37 GMT 12:37 GMT 
 Kieran Kelly 
Live reporter 
 Spoiler alert: This post contains a few details about the game. 
 New Zealander Connor Cattermoul has already completed GTA 6's introductory mission.
 The 27-year-old says it's "amazing" so far and has "beautiful" graphics, adding: "It feels really smooth - there's so many little things you can do."
 Those who have played previous instalments will know one of GTA's major appeals is its realism, which Connor says this version has maintained.
 Shortly after completing the 45-minute introduction, Connor headed straight to his character's in-game apartment and drank two beers before exploring the in-game version of Instagram.
 Connor was speaking to me at around 01:00 local time (12:00 GMT). He's still going to work tomorrow but plans to play the game every night through the weekend.
 Staying up was "pretty worth it", he says, adding that it "did not disappoint".
 Image source, Connor Cattermoul

 'It will be worth the wait,' says UK dad who took annual leave to play GTA published at 12:30 GMT 12:30 GMT 
 Rozina Sini 
Your Voice 
 Image source, Jason Waller Image caption, Grand Theft Auto 6 is not officially playable in the UK until midnight GMT on 19 November
 Jason Waller, 56, from Bedford, has booked two days of annual leave to play Grand Theft Auto 6 this weekend.
 "I love the freedom of GTA," he says. "You can leave the missions and wander off and discover so much."
 He says he and his son have both pre-downloaded the game ahead of its UK release.
 "We are going to put in an hour or two after midnight tonight and then play all day Friday and over the weekend."
 "If they’ve done it right it will be worth the wait. I can't wait," he says.

 New Zealand gamer shares first look at game (spoiler-free in this post) published at 12:23 GMT 12:23 GMT 
 Andrew Rogers 
BBC Newsbeat 
 Aleana Fernando, who lives in Auckland, New Zealand, gave BBC Newsbeat a first look at the game.
 So, her first impressions? Spoiler-free, of course.
 "The graphics are great. Even from the set-up and credits, it's feeling pretty good," she says.
 The 27-year-old says she’s going to play for a bit before getting some sleep ahead of work.
 She says it’s worth staying up, though, because it means so much to her for New Zealand to get the game first worldwide.
 "People sometimes forget about us, but it's nice to get a little bit of attention, especially with something this big."

 'It's a once in a generation kind of game' published at 12:07 GMT 12:07 GMT 
 Simon Atkinson 
Reporting from Sydney 
 I’m with YouTuber and gaming content creator Andrew Shelley - known to his one million followers and subscribers as Bombastic.
 He watched some of the GTA countdowns from New Zealand but turned off when the game began. "I want to see it fresh," he says, adding:
 "I'm so excited to play. It's 13 years waiting. So this is the moment. There's literally an hour to go. 
 "It's a once in a generation kind of game. There's so much more to it than so many other games. The scale of the world, the density, the satire of reality. 
 "I think they're just trying to capture so much in one giant game and have definitely taken the time to do so. So the anticipation of that's tremendous."

 GTA 6 attracts more than two million viewers on Twitch published at 12:00 GMT 12:00 GMT 
 Joe Coughlan 
Live editor 
 More than 2.4 million people are currently watching gamers play GTA 6 on Twitch, a website where people can watch and comment on others playing video games.
 Content creators are trying a variety of ways to attract viewers, including saying they’ll be the first to complete the game, playing it with their partners and giving away merchandise.
 For comparison, the second most popular category on Twitch is creators talking without playing a video game, with 136,000 viewers. The third most popular is World of Warcraft, with about 76,000 viewers.

 Trying to avoid spoilers? A twitch streamer has some tips published at 11:54 GMT 11:54 GMT 
 Jack Gray 
BBC Newsbeat 
 While gamers in New Zealand have started playing GTA 6, many of you in the UK are waiting patiently for it to drop here later tonight.
 Gaming livestreamer Alana Black, who you might know better as Alana CJ on Twitch, says she'll spend the day doing her best to avoid spoilers.
 "I just try to swipe past it, ignore it and don't peek at it,” she says.
 And her advice if you're trying to do the same? "Lock your phone away, turn off all devices, don't go near any social media.”
 The 30-year-old tells BBC Newsbeat she knows gamers who might be trying to use what's called the "New Zealand trick" to access the game early by changing their console's location.
 "You can be banned for it," she warns. "I wouldn't risk it personally. It's been 13 years since the last GTA, I can wait one more day."
 Image source, Alana Black

 'Exquisitely detailed' and 'mature': What the initial reviews are saying published at 11:46 GMT 11:46 GMT 
 Image source, Rockstar Games As we’ve just reported, reviews on Metacritic have given the game an average score of 99 .
 The New York Times , external has called the instalment a "dense game filled with friction", saying it "matures beyond its memorable car crashes and stick-ups with a game about love, relationships and nurturing your partner".
 Gaming website IGN , external has given the game a score of 10 out of 10, describing it as "exquisitely detailed" and "uncompromisingly engineered".
 The lowest confirmed reviews on the website currently give the game a score of 90.
 Meanwhile, entertainment outlet Slant Magazine , external says there are "flaws" in the game's creative approach in its four-and-a-half-star review, with its fantasy taking "power away from the player" at regular checkpoints.

 Pretending to be in New Zealand, booking leave and buying consoles - the lengths fans are going to published at 11:30 GMT 11:30 GMT 
 Laura Cress 
Technology reporter 
 Image source, Victoria Evans When Victoria Evans filed a leave request at work, the reason she gave was “GTA 6”. She told the BBC her boss "doesn't know what GTA 6 is".
 Anyway, the request was approved, and Victoria will get up at 05:00 GMT on Thursday to play, after its launch at midnight in the UK.
 She’s far from the only one. For the game’s launch day, HR software company BrightHR looked at absence data from more than 1.2 million employees at 70,000 businesses across the UK.
 It found GTA was mentioned in 4.6% of employees’ time-off requests.
 It said an estimated 83,000 days had been booked off for the game throughout November and December.
 Booking leave is only one way fans are making sure they’re ready for the big day.
 Others are buying a new console to play it on or even pretending they’re halfway around the world to get early access.

 GTA 6 gets almost perfect marks from reviewers published at 11:17 GMT 11:17 GMT Breaking 
 Tom Gerken 
Technology reporter 
 Image source, metacritic The reviews are in, and it appears the hype was for good reason.
 GTA 6 has an average review score of 99 on Metacritic , external , based on 100 critic reviews. 
 That means it’s - at least for now - tied for the top spot with the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which also scored 99 when it launched on the N64 in 1998.
 Not all the reviews may be in yet, so the final score could be a bit different.
 Some sites may want to experience more of the game before finalising their scores.
 But whatever the case, with countless reviewers giving GTA 6 perfect marks, this is a remarkable case of a game delivering on its truly monstrous hype.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 GTA 5 earned millions for Rockstar Games - can the sequel top it? published at 11:10 GMT 11:10 GMT 
 GTA 6’s predecessor was a record-breaker, and this new title is widely expected to be the biggest entertainment release ever.
 GTA 5 made Rockstar $1bn (£760m) in just three days after its release. Unsurprisingly, it holds the record for the best opening-week sales in video game history.
 The figure is on a par with the cost of developing GTA 6: estimates also put the cost of creating the game at about $1bn.
